- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) mid-period, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–3% for 2–4 days.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average of true values if sentiment is stable.
- If sentiment is uniformly low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model tends to underestimate; add 1–2% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
